properties.description: Grade II Listed.   Designed by Adrian Gilbert Scott.  Cruciform shape (120 feet by 120 feet) of steel girder and brick construction. Its Lantern tower – based on Ely Cathedral – is supported on parabolic arches 35 feet wide and 50 feet high.  The Stained Glass Windows were designed by John Wilson of Edinburgh and the Stations of the Cross  carved in Blue Horton Stone by Peter Watts.
properties.name: St Mary & St Joseph Roman Catholic Church, Poplar

properties.description:
Build a towering house of cards inspired by architects Charles and Ray Eames 1950s classic building toy- with  cards specially produced from Pollock's  vintage Toy Theatre scenery.  Create a 3D  paper garden to take home
Or join architect Ambrose Gillick to build  giant lightweight constructions.  Suitable for all .

images.title: Making and playing with MAPL (Pollock's Toy Museum)

properties.name: Pollocks House of Cards and Paper Gardens

properties.description: Explore the Generator House at RAF Uxbridge’s Battle of Britain Bunker. Normally off‑limits to the public, it houses the original 1930s standby generator that powered the underground Operations Room coordinating RAF Fighter Command in WWII. It offers a glimpse into wartime engineering, featuring preserved machinery, original fittings, and fascinating stories.  Free admission, no booking required.

images.title: The Battle of Britain Bunker - The Generator Hous

properties.name: The Battle of Britain Bunker - The Generator House

properties.description: Part of Manor Farm Heritage Site, The Great Barn is a Grade II listed  building and one of the oldest timber framed buildings of its type. Usually closed only for private events, the building as offers a glimpse into the rural history of the local area and is a testament to local craft and engineering.
properties.name: The Great Barn

properties.description: Manor Farm House in Ruislip, built in 1505–1507, is a Tudor-style, Grade II listed building that once hosted local court sessions and housed high-status guests. Now a visitor centre, it features original beams, historic displays, and forms part of the wider 22-acre Manor Farm heritage site.  It is also believed to be the home to the oldest example of surviving domestic English  wallpaper.

images.title: The Manor House, Manor Farm, Ruislip

properties.name: The Manor House, Manor Farm, Ruislip

properties.description: The dovecote at Eastcote House Gardens is an 18th-century, Grade II listed brick structure with a tiled roof, originally built to house pigeons for food and manure. It replaced an earlier Elizabethan dovecote by the Hawtrey family. Now preserved as part of  a tranquil gardens. Usually out-of-bounds to the public, it reflects historic manor life.
properties.name: The Dovecote, Eastcote House Gardens

properties.description: A Victorian Gothic Revival church hidden within Battersea's Shaftesbury Park Estate. Built in 1901 by architect G.H. Fellowes Prynne, it served the growing community before becoming a vibrant hub for Orthodox worship. Now home to a beautiful collection of icons donated from across the Orthodox world, alongside beautiful stained glass and original architectural details.
properties.name: Saint Nectarios Greek Orthodox Church

properties.description: The Royal Society of Musicians is a charity founded in 1738 with the express purpose to support music professionals. As such it is the oldest music-related charity in Great Britain. The Society has a rich archive, including an extensive collection of fine portraits, that are on display in its ground-floor meeting room in Fitzroy Square.

images.title: Paul Highnam; the Handel Room at The Royal Society of Musicians
Paul Highnam, exterior of 26 Fitzroy Square

properties.name: The Royal Society of Musicians of Great Britain

properties.description: A guided architecture walk exploring London’s post-war transformation, from the Brutalist vision of the Barbican to the High-tech Lloyd's Building and contemporary towers of the City. Through key landmarks, the tour reveals how social ideals, technological innovation, and economic change have shaped the modern skyline.
properties.name: Brutalism & High-Tech Architecture Tour

properties.description: Basil Scruby’s 1920’s-30’s classic Arts and Crafts style garden estate which was inspired by the character of the area’s woodland and rural open spaces. This guided walk of Petts Wood focuses on the contrasting house designs such as Tudor, Elizabethan and Art Deco including Charles Rene McIntosh influenced motifs. Stained glass also features at St Francis  church; a Nickolaus Pevsner listed historical building.

images.title: Woodland Way. Petts Wood.  Mel Wright
Poster 1930's Petts Wood & District Residents Association - fromHistory of Petts Wood. copyright2000

properties.name: Suburban Art and Design in Petts Wood

properties.description: Our school resides in a Grade II listed building on the edge of Hanworth Air Park. Fortescue House was the rectory for St. George's church on the edge of Hanworth Air Park. Later, it became a school, and now it is the home to the St. Michael Steiner School. We are blessed by beautiful grounds & woodland where the children can play & relax.  We enjoy the unique history and biodiversity of the area.

images.title: St Michael Steiner School - Lower School circle time

properties.name: The St Michael Steiner School

properties.description:
Herne Hill Velodrome, opened in 1891, hosted track cycling events for the 1948 Olympics, is now home to a thriving grassroots cycling facility - hosting everything from Learn to Cycle to local and international racing events. 
HHV overcame the threat of closure in the early 2000s, and a new pavilion, designed by Mike Taylor of Hopkins Architects, opened in 2017.
properties.name: Herne Hill Velodrome

properties.description: Eco Punk consists of a generous rear extension plus the remodel of an Edwardian house located in a conservation area. The new layout unlocks the spatial potentials. Besides beautifully crafted lounges, dining and utility areas, there is a kitchen that forms the centre piece. The latter is designed for a professional chef. An elegant, natural material palette ties the scheme together.
properties.name: Eco Punk

properties.description: This walking tour explores the City of London through the lens of nursery rhymes, using both well-known and lesser-known verses as a playful way into its architecture, communities and history. Rhymes such as 'London Bridge is Falling Down' and 'Oranges and Lemons' are rooted in real places and experiences. Along the way we will uncover some of the darker stories that may lie behind these innocent verses.
properties.name: Rhymes and Reasons: Exploring the City of London through nursery rhymes

properties.description: Built in 1776 for the Duke of Manchester to designs by John Crunden, Hertford House today holds the Wallace Collection. Join us in the Eranda Research Library to explore how an 18th century home developed into a world class museum. Discover our display of architectural drawings and prints, alongside items from the archive.

images.title: Hertford House - Ground Floor Plan c1897 (Wallace Collection)

properties.name: The Wallace Collection - Eranda Research Library

properties.description: As part of Open House 2026 in Croydon, visit an exhibition of our summer programme with Creative Quests: Curiosity Rover, and try some creative missions of your own! Part art studio, part community hub and part roaming spacecraft, collect quests to explore Croydon through noticing, movement, nature and imagination.
properties.name: Croydon Curiosity Rover

properties.description: Join us to explore the architectural history and future of the City of London's iconic glasshouse. Hear from the team behind Barbican Renewal, who will be restoring and revitalising the Conservatory from 2027-2030 with improvements to accessibility, sustainability and a new plant collection. Take part in a plant adoption event, leaving with a cutting from the Conservatory to grow at home.
properties.name: Barbican Conservatory

properties.description: This guided walking tour explores the social history of Tottenham — centred around Bruce Castle Park, Bruce Grove and Tottenham High Road — through three interconnected themes: drink, respectability and resistance. It examines how everyday spaces such as streets, homes, pubs and civic buildings were shaped by competing ideas about behaviour, morality and control.
properties.name: Drink, respectability and resistance

properties.description:
A Luis Barragán inspired design for the interior of a typical late Victorian house in East London. 
The use of bold vivid colour banishes the sterility that can accompany modernism without the loss of its hallmark simplicity and elegant line. This approach can be accommodated within houses whose external architecture has a very different heritage. Its achievement does not require a big budget
properties.name: 2 Belgrave Road: Victorian house with Luis Barragán inspired interior

properties.description: 18 Woolwich Road is a listed building known as the "Lodge", and part of the Greenwich Royal Hospital the entrance gatehouse of the third cemetery now a public park the Pleasaunce. The building is now a house occupied by Artist Fran Cottell who has added an extraordinary history using the house for her own work. A glazed roof to the rear addition has been designed by Elden Croy Architect.
properties.name: Open House 18 Woolwich Road

properties.description: The South Wing is a design-led Victorian home, location house and creative space in Croydon, shaped by a belief that beauty, atmosphere and thoughtful detail can change how people feel. For Open House, visitors are invited inside a private residential space that explores home as stage, sanctuary and cultural invitation.
properties.name: The South Wing

properties.description: This walking tour explores the different ways power and wealth is exemplified in architecture around the Strand. Inspired by the methods of Giovanni Battista Piranesi and his depiction of 'power' in his works, we will be doing sketches throughout the tour, studying different types of architectural components and ornamentation to help us imagine and compose our own impactful landscapes.

images.title: Collage of Piranesi's prison print and a photo of the Royal Courts of Justice taken by self

properties.name: Power in the eye of the beholder: Strand drawing tour

properties.description: This is a walking tour of the three acres, three new eco buildings and the eight glass houses on the Wolves Lane Centre site. This walking tour will include visiting the Palm House, with an abundance of exotic flora and fauna including lots of koi carp and terrapins, and the Cacti House which was started 18 years ago.

images.title: Overview of the Garden centre. Photographer Allistair Arendse

properties.name: Wolves Lane Centre

properties.description: Obra is Sordo Madaleno’s transdisciplinary laboratory, open library, and public living room, turning our London studio into a public-facing space for curiosity, testing, and dialogue. An addition to London's architectural landscape, Obra will host temporary exhibitions, events, and talks fostering exchange between the studio, the environments it works within, and the communities it engages.
properties.name: Obra

properties.description: St Michael's Chester Square is a grade 2 listed church in the heart of Victoria, built in the late Decorated Gothic style. The War Memorial Chapel at the north east end of the church was designed by Giles Gilbert Scott and completed in 1920. The stained glass West Window is by Hugh Easton and two windows to the south are by Morris & Co and date to 1882.
properties.name: St Michael's Chester Square

properties.description:
Lisson Grove Studios is a 1088m2 mixed use creative workspace hub providing permanent, affordable workspace for artists, designers, makers and small creative businesses.

The complex opened in February 2026 and includes 38 creative enterprise studios, a café, dance & rehearsal studio, 22 desk spaces, a meeting room, two phone booths and an exhibition space, arranged over 5 split level floors.
properties.name: Lisson Grove Studios

properties.description: Green Lodge is a low-energy family home by Stylus Architects, carefully embedded into the landscape of Putney Heath. Much of the accommodation is concealed below ground, allowing the building to maintain a modest presence whilst bringing natural light into every room through a series of lightwells and rooflights.

properties.description:
Paradise works artist studios in the Old Carbonic Works that is thought to be the birthplace of commercial fizzy drinks in the late 18th Century. It features in the Lea Valley and Hackney Conservation area report found online.


https://hackney.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s68747/240220%20Appendix%20A%20Lea%20Bridge%20Conservation%20Area%20Appraisal.pdf
properties.name: Former Carbonic Gas Works, 142 Lea Bridge Road

properties.description: A Great Fire Survivor, damaged in the blitz, the post war restoration of this fascinating building began 75 years ago this year.  Described by John Betjeman as a 'country church in the world of Seething Lane' the building uniquely blends medieval fabric with Festival of Britain era motifs. Explore the medieval crypt, 'Pepys' vestry, church tower and ringing room. Bellringing demonstrations.
properties.name: St Olave Hart Street

properties.description: Turning what was once a backland site into a two-storey, two-bedroom detached home, Wade House introduces a modern new-build to the heart of Metroland.
properties.name: Wade House

properties.description:
W House is a fully refurbished and extended house in Fulham. Various interventions have been made to create better visual connections and improve the flow through the house. 

The new volume at the rear of the house has been inspired by a series of pre-fabricated moulding details found in a historical joinery catalogue from a local craftsman that operated in the area during the Victorian times.
properties.name: W House

properties.description: The Avery Hill Winter Garden is a remarkable Victorian glasshouse set within the historic Avery Hill estate in southeast London. Built in the late 19th century, it was once home to an extensive collection of exotic plants and remains one of London’s largest surviving Victorian winter gardens.
properties.name: Avery Hill Winter Garden

properties.description: Right To Play is a celebration and a call to action to fight for our Right To Play. With bamboo den and structure building, Puppetry interaction, a "Long Table Mud Kitchen" play and a Run, Jump, Swing sculpture.
properties.name: Pif-Paf: Right To Play

properties.description: Explore Southlands Arts Centre and discover the history and architecture of this Grade II listed Queen Anne-style building. Admire its distinctive red-brick façade, elegant decorative detailing and historic interiors, and learn how this former private residence has evolved into a thriving community arts centre, celebrating Hillingdon's rich architectural and cultural heritage.

images.title: Southlands Arts Centre (The front façade of Southlands Art Centre)

properties.name: Southlands Arts Centre

properties.description: Be inspired by Croydon's space age buildings and aviation history - from Apollo and Lunar House, to Croydon Airport. Build your own models of familiar buildings redesigned as spacecrafts and transform the town centre into a space station.
properties.name: In Situ: Croydon Space Station

properties.description: As part of the weekend event Build /  Play / Shape Croydon, MATT+FIONA will lead a collaborative cardboard-build activity inspired by landmarks from Croydon's skyline. Visitors of all ages can help create a large scale installation using pre-made silhouette templates and recycled materials, contributing to "Croydon of the Future, Drawing on the Past".
properties.name: MATT + FIONA: Croydon Skyline

properties.description: Discover the hidden history of Cranford Park at this special open day. Explore the beautifully restored Grade II listed 18th-century stables and the secluded Secret Garden, once the estate's kitchen courtyard. Learn how these surviving buildings reveal life behind the scenes of the lost Cranford House estate and the ongoing conservation of this remarkable historic landscape.

images.title: Cranford Park - Stables and Secret Garden (Stables)

properties.name: Cranford Park - Stables and Secret Garden

properties.description: An architect-designed home exploring modern methods of construction through an exposed cross-laminated timber (CLT) structure. Designed and self-built as a low-energy contemporary home, it showcases how traditional craftsmanship and innovative timber engineering can create sustainable, beautifully crafted living spaces.
properties.name: Wood House

properties.description: Ibraaz is a London-based cultural institution for art, ideas, and dialogue from the Global Majority. Bringing together artists, thinkers, and communities through exhibitions, film, debate, publishing, and multidisciplinary programming, Ibraaz creates a brave space where culture fosters exchange, pluralism, and shared humanity.

images.title: Ibraaz at 93 Mortimer Street_2 (courtesy of Ibraaz; photo Vipul Sangoi)
Taring Padi_Rakyat Pasti Menang_Ibraaz (courtesy of the artist and Ibraaz; photo Ollie Hammick)

properties.name: Ibraaz

properties.description: Climb a ladder into the roof space above one of London's best-kept secrets and come face to face with Hawksmoor's beautiful ceiling. Explore Teulon's dramatic architecture, uncover tales of radical thinkers, pioneering doctors and inventive writers, and lose yourself in one of the capital's most secret churches. The roof space tour will be bookable on the day and you'll need to sign a disclaimer.
properties.name: Hidden ceilings & 300 years of secrets: SGTM Open Day

properties.description: Come and enjoy a circular 2-hour walk around Westminster, Whitehall and St James’ and hear about the events of one of the most tumultuous periods in London’s history, spanning the years 1603 (the death of Elizabeth I and arrival of James I), through Civil War, Regicide, Cromwell’s Republic, the Restoration right through to 1714 and the end of the Stuart Dynasty.

images.title: Statue of Oliver Cromwell outside of Westminster Hall - Alastair Mossman
Head of Charles I. Alastair Mossman

properties.name: Walk through the Stuart Dynasty and Cromwell’s Republic

properties.description: This is a walking tour that delves into the scandalous history of Covent Garden. This tour explores a time when the area served as London’s notorious red-light district, focusing on the lives of those forced into illicit trades or marginalized by the stringent moral laws of the day. The walk will share the stories of those who lived, worked and played in the area in days gone by.
